Use QUBO objective minimize -sum_i x_i + P * sum_{(i,j) in W} x_i x_j with penalty P > m. Any incompatible selection incurs at least penalty P while any feasible selection has penalty 0, so the optimum encodes a maximum-cardinality compatible subset. The required deterministic tie-break, smallest integer sum(2^i) over selected positions, is not naturally represented by this cardinality objective and must be resolved by an exact tie-breaking term or classical post-selection; this remains unresolved for approximate solvers.",
    "input_encoding": "One binary variable per eligible version: x_i in {0,1}. Ising mapping x_i=(1-Z_i)/2 if a spin formulation is used. Pairwise incompatibility penalties require O(m^2) coefficients derived from the classically constructed relation matrix.",
    "quantum_algorithm_family": "qaoa",
    "output_decoding": "Decode measured bitstrings into selected eligible version IDs in global version order. Recompute size, inactive status, compatibility, and missing_pairs using the original latest()/relation()/describe() logic. Verify feasibility and exact optimality, including the deterministic tie-break; if verification fails, do not emit the quantum result.",
    "assumptions": [
      "The classically constructed latest-check relation matrix and eligible ordering are available before encoding.",
      "Penalty P greater than the number of eligible versions is sufficient to make infeasible selections worse than all feasible selections.",
      "Data loading, oracle construction, workspace qubits, and decoding are not free and must be accounted for."
    ],
    "risks": [
      "QAOA/QUBO is not an exact solver; the software contract requires exact maximum size and exact tie-breaking, so heuristic output is not directly admissible.",
      "The deterministic tie-break smallest sum(2^i) may require exponentially small tie-breaking coefficients or exhaustive enumeration of optimal states.",
      "Insufficient penalty or approximate optimization can produce incompatible or non-maximum selections, violating the contract.",
      "No measured workload, hardware budget, or speedup evidence exists; classical brute force may remain preferable for this reporting function."
    ],
    "expected_resource_characteristics": {
      "num_qubits": "O(m) variable qubits plus ancillas for the oracle and constraints",
      "coefficient_count": "O(m^2) pairwise incompatibility penalties",
      "unresolved": "QAOA depth, parameter optimization budget, sampling overhead, and exact tie-breaking"
    },
    "rationale": "The select-mode loop is structurally a maximum pairwise-compatible subset problem, which can be expressed as QUBO/Ising. Exactness and tie-breaking obligations make a heuristic QAOA plan conditional and not a recommendation."
  },
  "rationale": "Lines 24-30 in program.py implement the only combinatorial optimization core: under mode=select, after prepare validation, latest_results construction, eligible active-version ordering, and relation matrix construction, the code enumerates every mask over eligible names, tests each subset with compatible(), and keeps the first maximum-size subset. Increasing mask order realizes the required tie-break by smallest integer sum(2^i). A migration must leave intact: prepare() validation and ValueError behavior for malformed fields, duplicate IDs, unknown IDs, bad current/members, and inspect/select modes; latest_results() last-record-wins semantics for undirected pairs including reversed pairs; eligible() preserving global version order and active-only membership; relation() treating only latest passed true as compatible; preview() greedy behavior staying unchanged; describe() reporting selected/inactive/missing_pairs/eligible_and_compatible consistently; and changes.add/remove preserving global version order. Structural eligibility is true because this is a maximum-cardinality pairwise-compatible subset problem expressible as QUBO/Ising. Practical suitability is false because the task requires exact maximum and deterministic tie-breaking, while the available combinatorial_optimization contract is approximate/heuristic and no workload evidence supports a benefit. Benchmark support is true only in the DRAFT shared-menu sense that a QUBO/Ising family exists, not as an approval or validated implementation.",
  "structural_eligibility": true,
  "practical_suitability": false,
  "benchmark_supported": true,
  "computational_intent": "Exact maximum-cardinality pair-compatible subset selection with deterministic smallest-integer-mask tie-breaking over active eligible release versions.",
  "assumptions": [
    "The latest pairwise check matrix and eligible ordering are computed classically before any quantum encoding.",
    "QAOA/QUBO can only be considered with exact post-verification because the contract forbids approximate size or compatibility.",
    "No free data loading, oracle construction, or decoding is assumed."
  ],
  "risks": [
    "Heuristic QUBO/QAOA optimizers may return incompatible or non-maximum selections.",
    "Exact tie-breaking by smallest sum(2^i) is not directly captured by cardinality QUBO and may be numerically fragile.",
    "Classical verification of exact optimality may be as expensive as the original exhaustive search, eliminating practical benefit.",
    "Replacing the loop without preserving validation, ordering, reporting, or changes semantics would violate the contract."
  ],
  "contract_applicability": [
    {
      "contract_id": "qubo-ising-v0",
      "applicable": true,
      "rationale": "The select-mode region is a binary optimization problem: maximize selected eligible versions subject to pairwise compatibility constraints. A QUBO/Ising penalty formulation is directly representable."
    },
    {
      "contract_id": "grover-predicate-v0",
      "applicable": false,
      "rationale": "The region is not a fixed pure predicate search; it is an optimization over all subsets with maximum cardinality and a deterministic tie-break. A fixed-size feasibility predicate could be constructed, but exact maximum/tie-breaking would require repeated searches and complex oracle logic, making this family a poor match."
    }
  ]
}
